subject: physical-education
title: Reteach and varied practice: the technical model for the second activity under transfer
focus: the technical model for the second activity
essentialQuestion: What transfers between two very different activities, and what does not?
materials: equipment for the second activity or a substitute
privacySafeScenario: Run a second documented development block in a contrasting activity and write a transfer analysis explaining what carried across from Pathway A and what did not.
studentTask: Learner works the technical model for the second activity run alongside the first specialization, where the two goals compete for the same time and the same recovery at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of the technical model for the second activity degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds the technical model for the second activity run alongside the first specialization, where the two goals compete for the same time and the same recovery, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: Contrast may be in category, environment, pace, or social structure; a learner with limited access chooses two contrasting home-based activities.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of the technical model for the second activity yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Contrast may be in category, environment, pace, or social structure; a learner with limited access chooses two contrasting home-based activities.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where the technical model for the second activity shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
